prize_parts.citation: For the design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and active sites

statement.case_for: Rational design of zeolite and related molecular-sieve catalysts is a complete chemical story: structure-directing agents and new frameworks (Davis, Zones), and catalyst design carried through to industrial refining, selective catalysis and emissions control (Corma, Zones). It has decades of independent confirmation and sustained industrial use, and it is chemistry at its centre (synthesis, structure, function) rather than a borderline case with physics or medicine. Corma, Davis and Zones cover synthesis, design and application, so a three-person award is defensible. The 2025 prize recognised extended coordination frameworks (MOFs), not aluminosilicate catalysts with Bronsted-acid sites and shape selectivity, so I do not see this as duplication.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that this is a broad field with many contributors, so a three-person cut (leaving out Tsapatsis and Jihong Yu, among others) is a judgment call, and the committee may see it as too close to the 2025 framework-materials prize. It currently has the least opening support on the shortlist, only my own first place, and the other seven members rank it low or not at all. I am also the member closest to porous-materials crystallography, so my enthusiasm should be discounted. Several other candidates (protein degradation, nucleic-acid delivery, sequencing chemistry) have clearer single concepts and broader opening support.

responses.point: Ranks targeted protein degradation (B020) first as a new, chemically induced-proximity modality, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the core, while noting the cereblon molecular-glue strand fits awkwardly into three names.
responses.response: I agree that the PROTAC concept is original and that Crews and Deshaies are the clearest founders. I ranked B020 only seventh because no degrader drug is approved yet and the credit is split across two mechanistic strands, as you note yourself. A three-name PROTAC-only prize would leave the thalidomide/cereblon work of Handa and Ito unrecognised, which I would not accept lightly. I would support B020 if the committee agrees it is mature enough, but I would not make it the first choice while clinical validation is still pending.

responses.point: Ranks halide perovskite solar absorbers (B005) first: a very clear first demonstration, rapid independent reproduction and a large impact, with credit spread over more than three people.
responses.response: I accept that perovskites have been reproduced very widely and that Miyasaka, Park and Snaith form the usual core. My reservation is attribution. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have real claims, and a trio that omits them will be disputed. The open questions about stability and lead toxicity also make the application story less settled than for zeolite catalysts, which have decades of industrial use behind them. I keep B005 as a serious alternative, but I place it behind a field whose maturity is easier to document.

responses.point: Ranks massively parallel sequencing (B014) second and argues that Balasubramanian and Klenerman form a coherent two-person core, while the field has several routes (Rothberg, Mayer, Ju).
responses.response: Reversible-terminator chemistry is a clear chemical invention and I see why you and Andrei Chabes value it. I am more cautious than the opening majority on the attribution: a prize limited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman would leave out the competing pyrosequencing and other platform routes that your own assessment describes as a genuine dispute, and adding Rothberg changes the claim to a technology-platform prize. I do not think that dispute is settled by the supplied record, so I treat B014 as strong but not yet ready.

responses.point: Ranks Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics (B053) first, with a clean two-person credit list and universal adoption, calling recognition overdue.
responses.response: Attribution is cleaner here than for almost any other shortlisted item, and the method has been tested for four decades, so on those two points I agree. The B053 case rests on method impact across computational chemistry, and I want to hear from colleagues whether the committee sees the 2013 multiscale-modelling prize and the 1998 density-functional recognition as already covering this ground. If they do not, I think B053 deserves to stay in the discussion alongside the molecular-sieve case.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards molecular-sieve catalyst design as one coherent discovery or a field too broad for a three-person award.
Whether the 2025 framework-materials prize makes porous-material candidates seem redundant to colleagues.
Relative credit among Corma, Davis and Zones, and whether Tsapatsis or Jihong Yu has a stronger claim than one of them; the supplied text does not settle it.
Whether clinical validation of protein degraders (B020) will mature enough to change my ranking.
statement.conflict_note: My research field (electron crystallography of zeolites and other porous crystals) is close to B044, and the structures of these frameworks are often solved with methods from my own area, so I flag a possible field-closeness issue and ask colleagues to weigh my advocacy accordingly. I have no known personal collaboration or institutional tie to Corma, Davis or Zones in the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which bears on none of the shortlisted candidates.
